name: Muda di Romania
notes: Schematic convoy spine through documented ports; not a claim of a single immutable track. Lane dates the galley auctions from 1329 and the Trebizond and Tana branches 1319-1322; the 1332 start sits inside that documented emergence and the end is the fall of Constantinople.

name: Muda di Alessandria
notes: Schematic convoy spine through the Adriatic and Cretan staging system. Round-century window is an envelope - the 1302 Mamluk treaty opened the run; the papal ban halted it 1322-1345; great galleys left commercial use soon after 1500 (Lane p348).

name: Muda di Siria
notes: Schematic Beirut and Syrian-market branch. The enduring four-route merchant-galley pattern including Cyprus-or-Syria dates from the late fourteenth century (Lane p131); round-century window is an envelope.

name: Muda di Cipro
notes: Schematic Cyprus convoy branch. Cyprus was at times a terminus of regulated fleets from the early fourteenth century (Lane p130); round-century window is an envelope.

name: Muda di Dalmazia
notes: Schematic coastal service linking Venetian Dalmatia. Editorial window keyed to the 1409-1420 possession phase - Lane documents no scheduled Dalmatia muda before the Spalato line begun after 1577 and auctioned from 1592 (p303).

name: Adriatic round-ship trade
notes: Representative private navigation corridor rather than a scheduled muda. Thirteenth-century caravan convoy system per Lane pp68-70.

name: Aegean round-ship trade
notes: Representative private navigation corridor through Venetian and feudatory ports. Start aligned to the corrected 1206 possession of Modon and Coron (O'Connell p19).
